summary.en: Songwriters, the studio band, etiquette coaches, choreographers, and label management together form the Motown assembly line.
summary.zh: 歌曲作者、录音室乐队、礼仪教练、编舞人员和厂牌的经营管理结合在一起，组成了Motown流水线。

body.zh:
歌曲作者、录音室乐队、礼仪教练、编舞人员和厂牌的经营管理结合在一起，组成了Motown流水线。

现在让我们来谈谈Motown出品的音乐。Motown开始自称Hitsville, USA（美国热单镇），后来被人们称作Motown。1959年，Berry Gordy Jr.在底特律创办了Motown。在黑人音乐事业发展的历程中，Berry Gordy Jr.是一个非常重要的人物。我并不确定这个说法现在是否依然正确：Motown唱片是美国黑人经营的公司中最成功的。刚开始它是以地区性独立厂牌形式出现的，后来成为了流行音乐界的一股强大力量。它成功的原因，一部分是因为它的旗下艺人和做事情的人很出色；一部分是因为Berry Gordy Jr.个人的眼光，他最初就有办厂牌吸引白人听众的想法，他想让他的团队拥有尽量广泛的听众群。
先说说Berry Gordy Jr.的个人经历吧。他曾经是一名职业拳击手，经常与其他拳击手们以及底特律爵士酒吧里的爵士音乐人交往。Motown是在密歇根州的底特律创办的，Berry的生活基本是在健身馆与拳击手们交往，以及在俱乐部和爵士音乐家们交往，他还一度在一家汽车公司的流水线上工作。Berry Gordy Jr.进军音乐界的第一个举动，是开了一家专营爵士乐的唱片店。正如许多热爱音乐的人一样，他的想法是，既然爵士乐是最好的，那我就卖爵士乐。然而他发现，很多时候人们并不想买那些发烧友或是专家们认为最好的音乐，只有卖最流行的音乐才能真正赚到钱。但Berry Gordy说，直到他的爵士音乐店已经失败到无法挽回的时候，他才意识到卖流行乐或R&B才能真正赚钱。因此，他开始调整策略，时刻牢记流行音乐才是赚钱之道。
Berry Gordy Jr.通过写歌来继续音乐事业。他起初为Jackie Wilson写歌，包括在1957年发行的《Reet Petite》，1958年的《Lonely Teardrops》在R&B榜单上名列第一，同时在流行音乐榜上排名第七，1959年《That’s Why I Love You So》在R&B榜单上排名第二。这些都是Berry Gordy Jr.作为一个创作者与他人合作的代表作。Jerry Leiber的熟人告诉我，Berry Gordy Jr.曾和Jerry Leiber交流过关于Leiber & Stoller的歌曲制作团队的事，他说他希望加入Brill Building。我们之前讲过这种商业模式在五十年代后期开始形成，在六十年代走向繁荣。于是Jerry Libber问Berry你为什么想要在纽约从头开始你的事业呢？你在底特律已经取得一些不错的成绩了，你为什么不在这里做你想做的事呢？于是Berry Gordy Jr.听取了他的建议，并在1959年成立了Motown唱片公司。
Motown的模式在许多方面都与Brill Building的模式相似，除了在63、64、65年的时候，Brill Building从六十年代初的辉煌开始衰落，许多制作人都搬到了西海岸。比如说Don Kirshner等音乐人将重心转移到了洛杉矶。但就在六十年代中后期的这段时间，Motown将Brill Building的模式搬到了底特律。确实基于Brill Building模式，Motown在这期间迅速发展。早期Berry Gordy在Motown发行的金曲有Barrett Strong的《Money》，在1960年登上R&B榜第二位。我们继续谈谈与Brill Building同时代发生的事情。1960年，女子组合The Marvellettes演唱的《Please Mr. Postman》同时在流行榜和R&B榜上排名第一。一个小型地方厂牌发行了热门单曲，这是很大的成功。The Contours有首歌叫做《Do You Love Me》，在1962年排在了R&B榜第一和流行榜第三。早期Berry Gordon的唱片发行的时候，从许多方面看都模仿了其他人的作品。The Marvelettes就是一个1961年诞生的女子组合，The Contours听上去像1962年的The Isley Brothers。所以说在起步阶段，Berry Gordy也追随了其他人的脚步。
现在我们来聊聊关于跨界和吸收白人听众的理念。如果你是一个注意行业发展趋势的商人，关注可支配收入的流动方向，关注有闲钱购买唱片的人们，很明显，大部分的钱都掌握在白人手中。正如我之前提到的，Berry Gordy在爵士音乐店时期就决定要吸引白人听众，他坚信如果想取得事业的成功，就必须这样做。但他旗下的许多艺人们都出身中等或是贫穷的家庭，他们并不像那些即使没有受过训练也可以融入上流社会的人。因此他需要想办法来重塑这些艺人，打造Motown的形象，使它能够被白人听众接受。正如我之前说过，许多人批判这种行为，视之为某种程度上的背叛。但事实上，这就像Chuck Berry在1955、56、57年直接写歌给白人少年听众，从而使黑人R&B不需要改词再翻唱也能被接受。因此我们可以认为Motown唱片的早期阶段，运用了Chuck Berry哲学，并采取了Brill Building的模式，将它们融合在一起，从而使它成为底特律的一个非常成功的厂牌。
我们来了解下Motown的礼仪课和编舞。Motown的不同之处在于，人们喜欢将它视作流水线。我认为这一部分是因为 Motown在底特律，而底特律在彼时是汽车工业的发源地，任何人谈到底特律都会想到福特、通用、克莱斯勒这些大型汽车公司。通过分工将音乐制作分成各个不同的工种的想法，与流水线的工作方法如出一辙。当然，Brill Building或是大部分纽约厂牌也很像流水线。正如我之前说过，Berry Gordy Jr.对于厂牌形象以及旗下明星的公众行为感到担忧，所以他雇了Maxine Powell女士来教一门被艺人们称为“礼仪学校”的课程。Maxine Powell也确实在五十年代的底特律曾经营一所礼仪学校，她的工作就是教导这些出身贫寒的人们如何在用餐时正确使用餐具，如何拥有优雅的谈吐和恰当的措辞，如何优美地动作、走路，她还教导女士上车的时候要注意合拢双腿，吃东西的时候要闭着嘴巴。这些事情是父母一直要求孩子们做的，并不是所有的艺人都面临这些问题。但Berry Gordy说，他的目标是让他手下的所有艺人都可以在两个地方出席：白宫和白金汉宫。因此教授他们礼仪并不是为了让他们日常交往，这更像是当与美国总统或是英国女王同席时，他们能够表现得体，并达到优雅的标准。而Maxine Powell的工作就是教导Motown旗下的所有艺人，确保他们达到这样的水平。大部分艺人当时都是年轻人，他们都十分痛恨这个课程。但多年以后，许多人都对从Maxine Powell那里得到的训练表示感激，因为这确实对他们之后的事业有很大帮助。Berry做的另一件事，是雇了曾在百老汇编舞的Cholly Atkins来为所有的表演编舞。所以你看到的各个组合的每一个舞蹈动作，比如说The Supremes、Four Tops 还有The Temptations舞蹈的动作，都是由Cholly Atkins探索完成的。那么你就已经知道，Motown的礼仪由一个人负责，编舞由另一个人负责，而且Motown也负责艺人的管理，协调艺人的宣传活动、唱片发行和巡演，在巡演中把很多组合集中在一起。因此Berry Gordy确实创造出一个造星工厂，他充分控制着对旗下艺人事业的塑造。
从音乐的角度来看，Motown流水线一方面是由歌曲作者和制作人组成的，另一方面，录音室乐队的成员为所有的唱片伴奏。通过模仿Brill Building模式，Berry Gordy拥有了一个由歌曲作者和制作人组成的团队，这些人都会写歌，为得到下一张唱片的制作而较劲。Berry经常会把他们召集起来开会，讨论他们都有哪些歌曲。Berry Gordy经常会问，如果你只有一美元，你愿意买这张唱片还是三明治？所以他发行的唱片，或者说他们决定录制的唱，一定要好到人们愿意不吃午餐也要买它的程度，这就是他分辨一张唱片是“好”还是“极好”的方法。所以歌曲作者和制作人们都为了得到每周的唱片制作权而互相竞争。得胜的人可以选择为一个艺人打造唱片，只要他们负责的艺人一直星途坦荡，他们就可以继续负责，一旦这个艺人的事业下滑，那么其他的制作人就有机会来接手，来保证这个艺人在榜单上名列前茅。我们提到的一些制作人和歌曲作者，如Berry Gordy Jr.、Mickey Stevenson、Smokey Robinson，都是一些非常有影响力的歌曲作者。还有一些歌曲制作团队，如Brian Holland、Lamont Dozier、Eddie Holland，我们经常叫他们Holland Dozier Holland，或者直接叫成HDH，还有Norman Whitfield。这些人都在Motown最鼎盛的六十年代写歌和制作。
他们也有一支录音室乐队，叫做The Funk Brothers，他们是洛杉矶的The Wrecking Crew的底特律版。The Wrecking Crew是一群为Phil Spector唱片演奏的顶级录音室音乐人，他们为The Byrds的《Mr. Tambourine Man》和The Beach Boys的唱片伴奏。在底特律，The Funk Brothers是Motown的专属乐队。你们可能知道一部2002年的电影《Standing in the Shadows of Motown》，这是一部真正关于Motown背后的那些无名英雄的纪录片，他们与歌曲创作者、制作人和艺人的工作都十分密切，许多关于他们的事情都没有被记录下来，他们会跟随着音乐，完成自己的任务。我们谈论的是贝斯手James Jamerson、鼓手Bennie Benjamin、钢琴手Earl Van Dyke以及许许多多这样的人。Motown拥有自己专门的录音室，这个录音室几乎一直都在被使用，所以一个乐队无法完成所有任务。但是还是有一组核心乐手，当核心乐队的成员需要休息或是要去其他地方演出时，其他的乐手会替补上来。
因此，歌曲作者、录音室乐队、礼仪教练、编舞人员和经营管理综合在一起，被认为是Motown流水线。当然，唯一一个我们还没说的部分就是演出者，他们正是观众所注目的焦点，下节课我们就来说说Motown的歌手们。
body.en:
Songwriters, the studio band, etiquette coaches, choreographers, and label management together form the Motown assembly line.

Now Motown’s music. Motown first calls itself Hitsville, U.S.A.; later people simply say Motown. In 1959 Berry Gordy Jr. founds Motown in Detroit. In the history of Black music business he is a major figure. I am not sure this still holds: Motown Records as the most successful Black-owned company in America. It begins as a regional indie and becomes a major force in pop. Part of the success is outstanding artists and staff; part is Gordy’s own eye—from the start he wants a label that draws white listeners and the widest possible audience.
Start with Gordy’s own path. He was a pro boxer, mixing with other fighters and with jazz musicians in Detroit jazz clubs. Motown is founded in Detroit, Michigan; Berry’s life is gyms and boxers, clubs and jazz players—and for a time work on an auto assembly line. His first move into music is a jazz record shop. Like many music lovers, he figures: jazz is the best, so sell jazz. He finds people often do not buy what aficionados or experts call best; only the most popular music truly makes money. Gordy says he only grasped that selling pop or R&B was the real money after the jazz shop had already failed past repair. So he adjusts strategy, keeping pop as the path to profit.
He continues through songwriting. Early on he writes for Jackie Wilson, including 1957’s “Reet Petite”; 1958’s “Lonely Teardrops” hits No. 1 R&B and No. 7 pop; 1959’s “That’s Why I Love You So” reaches No. 2 R&B. These are representative Gordy co-writes. An acquaintance of Jerry Leiber told me Gordy once talked with Leiber about the Leiber & Stoller production team and said he hoped to join the Brill Building. We have covered that business model forming in the late 1950s and flourishing in the 1960s. Jerry Leiber asks why start from scratch in New York when you already have results in Detroit—why not do what you want here? Gordy takes the advice and founds Motown in 1959.
In many ways Motown’s model resembles Brill Building’s—except that by 1963–65 Brill Building fades from its early-1960s peak and many producers move west; Don Kirshner and others shift to Los Angeles. In that mid-to-late-1960s stretch Motown transplants the Brill Building model to Detroit. Built on that model, Motown grows fast. Early Gordy Motown hits include Barrett Strong’s “Money,” No. 2 R&B in 1960. Alongside Brill-era developments: in 1960 the girl group the Marvelettes’ “Please Mr. Postman” hits No. 1 pop and R&B. A small local label with a smash—major success. The Contours’ “Do You Love Me” is No. 1 R&B and No. 3 pop in 1962. Early Berry Gordy releases, in many ways, imitate others: the Marvelettes are a 1961 girl group; the Contours sound like 1962 Isley Brothers. At the start Gordy also follows others’ footsteps.
Now crossover and courting white listeners. If you watch industry trends, disposable income, and who has money for records, most of the money is clearly in white hands. As noted, from the jazz-shop period Gordy decides to attract white listeners; he believes success requires it. But many of his artists come from middling or poor families; they are not people who can move in high society without training. So he needs ways to reshape them and Motown’s image so white audiences will accept them. As I said, many criticize this as a kind of betrayal. In fact it is like Chuck Berry in 1955–57 writing straight to white teenage listeners so Black R&B need not be rewritten and covered to be accepted. Early Motown can be read as Chuck Berry’s philosophy plus the Brill Building model, fused into a highly successful Detroit label.
Etiquette class and choreography. Motown’s difference is that people like to see it as an assembly line—partly because Motown is in Detroit, then the auto capital: Ford, GM, Chrysler. Dividing music-making into specialized jobs mirrors assembly-line method. Of course Brill Building and most New York labels are assembly-like too. As noted, Gordy worries about label image and artists’ public behavior, so he hires Maxine Powell to teach what artists call “finishing school.” Powell had run an etiquette school in 1950s Detroit; her job is to teach people from poor backgrounds how to use utensils, speak with grace and proper wording, move and walk well—ladies closing their knees when getting into a car, chewing with mouths closed. Things parents always ask of children; not every artist has these problems. But Gordy says his goal is that every artist can appear in two places: the White House and Buckingham Palace. Etiquette is not for daily life so much as for sitting with a U.S. president or the British queen with proper grace. Powell’s work is to teach all Motown artists to that standard. Most are young and hate the class. Years later many thank the training; it helps their careers. Gordy also hires Broadway choreographer Cholly Atkins for all acts. Every dance move you see from the Supremes, Four Tops, Temptations is Atkins’s work. So etiquette is one person, choreography another; Motown also manages artists—promotion, releases, tours that package many acts together. Gordy truly builds a star factory and fully shapes careers.
Musically the Motown line is songwriters and producers on one side, studio players backing every record on the other. Imitating Brill Building, Gordy has a team of writers and producers competing for the next production. He often calls meetings to hear what songs they have. He asks: if you have only a dollar, do you buy this record or a sandwich? Records they choose to cut must be good enough that people skip lunch to buy them—that is how he separates “good” from “great.” Writers and producers compete weekly for production slots. Winners may craft records for an artist; as long as that artist stays hot they keep the assignment; if the career dips, another producer can take over to keep the charts. Influential writers and producers include Gordy, Mickey Stevenson, Smokey Robinson; teams such as Brian Holland, Lamont Dozier, Eddie Holland—Holland–Dozier–Holland, or HDH—and Norman Whitfield. They write and produce through Motown’s peak 1960s.
There is also a studio band, the Funk Brothers—Detroit’s answer to L.A.’s Wrecking Crew. The Wrecking Crew play for Phil Spector, on the Byrds’ “Mr. Tambourine Man,” Beach Boys records. In Detroit the Funk Brothers are Motown’s house band. You may know the 2002 film Standing in the Shadows of Motown—a documentary on Motown’s unsung heroes, working closely with writers, producers, and artists, much of it poorly documented; they follow the music and do their jobs. Bass James Jamerson, drums Benny Benjamin, piano Earl Van Dyke, and many others. Motown has its own studio in near-constant use, so one band cannot cover everything. Still there is a core; when core players rest or tour, others fill in.
Thus songwriters, studio band, etiquette coaches, choreographers, and management together are called the Motown assembly line. The one piece still missing is the performers—the focus of the audience. Next: Motown’s singers.
